scope: MAX/MXene XPS request generation, defect/dopant-aware interpretation, quantification, and vendor-vs-Python QC
principles: Do not infer a unique chemical state from binding energy alone when multiple local environments can produce similar shifts.
Keep composition change, M-site vacancy, X-site vacancy, termination vacancy/disorder, dopant incorporation, oxidation, and secondary phases as separate latent variables.
For mixed-metal MXenes, do not renormalize the metal sublattice to the ideal M count before computing an apparent metal-deficiency index; that would erase the quantity of interest.
Treat XPS-derived vacancy concentration as apparent/surface-sensitive unless independently supported by STEM/EELS/ICP/EDS or another orthogonal method.
Keep raw and model-corrected termination estimates side-by-side; corrections must be explicit and switchable.

notes: Primary interpretation follows Brette et al.; Ti 2p shifts should not be mapped one-to-one onto oxidation states.
O 1s near 531 eV can reflect disordered/mixed termination environments and termination vacancies; do not automatically call it OH.
F 1s is comparatively insensitive to local environment; a single MXene-F contribution can represent multiple local configurations.
Brette2024 identified a single F 1s contribution in HF10 and HF48 spectra; no F residue value is reported there.

notes: This is a conservative composite profile assembled from Ti-Nb solid-solution, Nb-vacancy, and Ti3C2 XPS references; no single cited paper uniquely resolves all variables in a defect-rich (Nb,Ti)2CTx sample.
Fit Ti 2p and Nb 3d independently, then integrate the interpretation across C 1s/O 1s/F 1s and composition data.
Do not force a vacancy-specific peak. Report selective Ti/Nb depletion and apparent M-site deficiency separately from absolute vacancy concentration.
For O 1s, mixed Ti/Nb oxides and terminations overlap. Component roles should remain provisional until Ti/Nb core-level consistency is checked.

rules.framework_Ti: Sum C-Ti+1-Tx, C-Ti+2-Tx, C-Ti+3-Tx; exclude TiO2-xF2x(Ti)
rules.O_termination: low-BE O + optional high-BE O component
rules.F_oxide_correction: F_corr = max(0, F_raw - O_oxide * factor), legacy factor 0.6667
rules.normalization: Scale by 2 / framework_C, then compare Ti_norm with 3
rules.QC: Ti_norm within 3 +/- 0.5; corrected z_total between 1 and 3

Ti2-yNbyCTx.note: Published XPS stoichiometries were normalized using one theoretical metal amount; useful for composition trends but not as an absolute vacancy calibration.

validation_defaults.note: Thresholds are conservative QC defaults, not literature constants; expose them to the user. Brette et al. estimate ~0.5 eV numerical uncertainty for their DFT BE calculations and note experimental resolutions around ~0.3 eV in cited MXene work.
